added_lemmas.justification: This theorem supplies a fully private, finite-sample honest upper bound on the unchanged full positive-density class by using only fixed-dimensional local regressions.
added_lemmas.gap: The higher-order construction is proved only on the attainable uniform-design submodel; this direct construction gives a nonsharp but valid full-class endpoint without importing those design identities.
added_lemmas.consumer: An investigator can release a pointwise CATE interval under unknown bounded design density with a certified mean-length rate, while treating the sharper nuisance-adaptive frontier as unresolved.

added_lemmas.justification: The proposition records the strongest currently certified two-sided full-class result rather than leaving the upper endpoint at the trivial length two.
added_lemmas.gap: The lower endpoint uses the smoother contrast, while the direct upper endpoint uses the rougher arm-regression smoothness, so the exact private modulus is not identified.
added_lemmas.consumer: The bracket gives reviewers and privacy-budget committees a valid range for the optimal mean interval length on one unchanged law class.

proposed_statement_changes.reason: The old radius condition was unnecessarily strong.  The same two-law witness can use the constant propensity \(\pi_Q\equiv\kappa\), whose Hölder norm is \(\kappa\), so the explicitly directed compatibility condition \(L_\pi\ge\kappa\) suffices while the two exponents and privacy saturation are unchanged.

proposed_definition_changes.reason: The handle must incorporate the newly certified full-class direct-regression endpoint while preserving the paired-cell and stabilized higher-order routes as questions about sharpness rather than as established results.

proposed.justification: This theorem separates the sound full-class privacy limitation from both the attainable-submodel higher-order upper and the nonsharp full-class direct-regression upper.
proposed.gap: Existing private pointwise regression bounds concern noncausal regression experiments; the theorem embeds that barrier into honest causal intervals on the unchanged positive-density class with the weakest constant-propensity radius compatibility used by its witness.
proposed.consumer: Reviewers and privacy-budget committees obtain a defensible lower benchmark without relying on the rejected paired-microcell transport argument.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This complete post-image applies the directed radius repair, adds \(\kappa\) and \(q\) to the free-symbol set, removes the unused attainable-inclusion dependency, and synchronizes the theorem notes.

proposed.justification: The remaining gap is between the ordinary \(\gamma\)-smooth lower endpoint and the new \(\beta\)-smooth direct-regression upper endpoint on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\); the higher-order achieved phase remains confined to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).
proposed.gap: Neither KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 nor the located private CATE and private confidence-interval papers characterize the privacy-constrained confidence modulus between these two full-class endpoints.
proposed.consumer: A resolution determines whether private heterogeneous-treatment-effect studies on the full unknown-density class pay only an ordinary local-regression privacy price or can exploit the smoother contrast or nuisance interaction.

obligation.what_is_open: Determine whether a paired-microcell fuzzy family admits an \(n\)-sample coupling with sufficiently small expected Hamming cost, or construct a private stabilized higher-order estimator that improves the fixed-dimensional \(\beta\)-smooth upper on the full unknown-density class.
obligation.obstruction: The one-cell cancellation does not control repeat-cell dependence in the prior mixture.  The new direct estimator avoids pilots and unknown-density Gram identities, but its armwise Taylor bias is only \(O(h^\beta)\); no full-class private higher-order stabilization has been proved.
obligation.attempted: The ordinary causal bump lower, approximate-DP Hamming transport, one-cell cancellation audit, attainable-class envelope optimization, and the all-observation private direct-regression upper have been completed.  These yield a nontrivial full-class bracket but do not identify its sharp endpoint.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The formal question is unchanged, but its dependency spine and notes must include the new direct-regression theorem and the resulting nonsharp full-class bracket.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Determine whether a paired-microcell fuzzy family admits an \(n\)-sample coupling with sufficiently small expected Hamming cost, or construct a private stabilized higher-order estimator that improves the fixed-dimensional \(\beta\)-smooth upper on the full unknown-density class.
open_obligations.obstruction: The one-cell identity cancels the one-observation prior mixture but does not control dependencies caused by repeat visits to a latent microcell.  The direct full-class learner now supplies a valid upper endpoint, but its armwise local-polynomial bias is \(O(h^\beta)\), and no private higher-order Gram or propose-test-release argument has improved that endpoint on the same class.
open_obligations.attempted: I retained the proved Hamming-transport reduction and ordinary \(\gamma\)-bump lower, checked the paired-cell cancellation obstruction, and constructed an all-observation joint Gaussian release of both arm-specific local-polynomial Grams and moments with a spectral-floor fallback.  The resulting full-class upper closes the trivial endpoint but does not decide sharpness.

prose_updates.tldr: The paper constructs a replacement-private, finite-sample honest pointwise CATE interval on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), the uniform-design attainable submodel.  Projected private spline pilots, a clipped higher-order local moment, joint Gaussian releases, and spectral stabilization yield the achieved phase-sensitive length upper \(1\wedge(r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}})\) there; this is not transferred to the full class.  On \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\), a separate all-observation, fixed-dimensional private direct-regression interval is honest and has the nonsharp \(\beta\)-smooth upper \(1\wedge\{n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}\vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}\}\).  Together with the ordinary \(\gamma\)-smooth lower bound, this replaces the trivial length-two endpoint by a nontrivial full-class bracket while leaving the exact private confidence modulus open.

project_justification.fill: The project privatizes every pilot and localized moment for the attainable higher-order construction, proves unrestricted-finite-rank concentration, uniform finite-sample coverage, and the phase-sensitive mean interval length upper \(1\wedge(r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}})\) on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).  Separately, it proves both an ordinary regression lower limitation and an explicit fixed-dimensional direct-regression upper on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  Under \(L_\pi\ge\kappa\), \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), and sufficiently large \(n\), the full-class bracket is \(c[n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\vee\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\}]\le\mathcal L_n^*(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}})\le C[1\wedge\{n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}\vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}\}]\).  The attainable higher-order upper is not transferred to the full class, and exact sharpness remains unresolved.

prose_updates.related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024) establish the privacy-free pointwise CATE rate and motivate the higher-order local-polynomial architecture.  Their upper theorem requires its stated design-density and population-Gram conditions; this paper verifies the needed higher-order identities only for its uniform-design attainable construction and does not assert that the KBRW upper transfers to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  Nor is KBRW's density-hole fuzzy lower asserted to transfer to the present full class with a positive anchor density band.  The new full-class result instead uses standard fixed-dimensional direct regression: overlap and the local density band condition the two population Grams, while armwise \(\beta\)-smooth Taylor bias yields a deliberately nonsharp private upper.  Robins, Li, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart (2008) supply the higher-order influence-function perspective behind the attainable quadratic correction.  Armstrong and Kolesár (2020) motivate honest fixed-length intervals that expose worst-case smoothing bias.  Lee, Okui, and Whang (2017) provide nonprivate doubly robust CATE bands in a lower-dimensional heterogeneity problem.  Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel (2025) study private orthogonal CATE learning but do not derive this pointwise Hölder coverage and length phase; Schröder, Hartenstein, and Feuerriegel (2025) treat private intervals for the regular population ATE.  Shoham, Shenfeld, Velner-Harris, and Ligett (2026) give an asymptotic resampling conversion for private estimators, whereas the present intervals use explicit uniform finite-sample bias control.  Dwork and Roth (2014) provide the Gaussian mechanism and post-processing fact used by both private constructions.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The higher-order privacy term comes from the global sensitivity \(m^{-1}(h^{-d}+kh^{-2d})\) of the clipped quadratic-moment release and is proved only as an attainable-submodel upper cost.  The separate full-class direct-regression release has sensitivity \(O((nh^d)^{-1})\) but incurs armwise bias \(O(h^\beta)\), so it does not determine whether the smoother \(\gamma\)-contrast, the nuisance interaction \(q\), or a stabilized private Gram controls the sharp frontier.  The invalid paired-microcell transport step is not revived.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Settled results are replacement privacy and uniform finite-sample coverage of the explicit higher-order interval on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), its achieved length upper \(1\wedge(r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}})\), the corrected construction-specific privacy-free reduction with no rank floor, the ordinary full-class lower limitation, and the new fixed-dimensional direct-regression coverage and upper bound on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  The attainable class is restricted to uniform design; its higher-order upper is not transferred to the full class.  Under \(L_\pi\ge\kappa\), \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), and sufficiently large \(n\), the settled full-class result is \(c[n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\vee\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\}]\le\mathcal L_n^*(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}})\le C[1\wedge\{n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}\vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}\}]\).  Whether this bracket is tight, including whether a \(q\)-driven or private-Gram branch is unavoidable, remains the open-ended question.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem supplies the ordinary \(\gamma\)-smooth lower endpoint on the full class and now requires only the constant-propensity compatibility \(L_\pi\ge\kappa\).
statement_notes.gap: The two-law witness proves no \(q<\gamma\) paired-cell term, so it remains a lower benchmark rather than the full frontier.
statement_notes.consumer: Reviewers and privacy-budget committees can compare any full-class private interval against a causal lower bound that uses strictly positive common-support outcomes.

statement_notes.justification: The remaining gap is between the ordinary \(\gamma\)-smooth lower endpoint and the new \(\beta\)-smooth direct-regression upper endpoint on the same full class; the higher-order achieved phase remains confined to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).
statement_notes.gap: No proved coupling or stabilized higher-order full-class release decides whether the optimal privacy branch is governed by \(\gamma\), \(q\), or a private Gram.
statement_notes.consumer: A resolution would determine which privacy budget is sufficient for pointwise heterogeneous-treatment-effect inference under unknown bounded design density.
